title: Add the combined engine and client install mode
summary: The Forgel Code installer, run with no extra flags, installs the engine alongside the client, so the documented one-command install yields a working pair. It is idempotent by comparing the installed engine against the version the configured engine source provides: no engine installs it, an installed engine at or above the available one is kept untouched, a strictly newer available engine replaces it, and the finished result always satisfies the declared minimum, failing with an actionable message when it cannot. The default engine source is a documented configuration, and the run reports which engine version is installed.
plan_goal: Make Forgel and Forgel Code install and run as one working pair: give the engine `forgel` its own installer, add a mode of the Forgel Code installer that installs both binaries together (offered by default in the README, idempotent — when the engine is already present it compares versions and installs only a strictly newer one), and introduce a declared minimum supported engine version for Forgel Code, checked at startup, so a missing or too-old engine produces a clear actionable message instead of `engine forgel: executable not found: forgel`.

checks.criterion: A run with no extra options installs the client and the available engine and states it as newly installed.
The client-only option installs no engine.
The available engine version is known before any engine is installed and drives the decision.
A present engine at or above the available version is left unchanged.
A strictly newer available version replaces an older present engine.
An available version below the declared minimum fails without installing and names the minimum and the available version.
A present engine below the declared minimum with no newer available version fails and names the minimum and the present version.
Failure messages name the required minimum and an actionable next step.
A second identical run installs no engine and states the same version.
Changing the configured engine source changes the version considered available.
An unreachable engine source fails with an actionable message and leaves the present engine untouched.
A failed engine installation leaves the client installed and ends as a failure with an actionable message.
An engine that cannot report its version is treated as missing.
The behavior the client installation had before this change is preserved.

external_dependencies.name: engine installation and version reporting supplied by the engine
external_dependencies.interface: The client never imports engine internals. It uses three operations behind one seam: (1) probe the configured engine source for the version it offers, without installing anything -> Version | None; (2) install a chosen version from that source -> void; (3) read the version the installed engine itself declares -> Version | None. Reconciliation on top of them: nothing installed -> install the available version; installed >= available -> keep untouched; available > installed -> install the available one; afterwards assert installed >= declared minimum and fail with an actionable message otherwise. The run reports the resulting installed version. Every operation is deterministic: no network, no clock, no ambient state; versions are compared as (major, minor, patch).
external_dependencies.docs: Task specification in the repository (behaviour of the combined install mode: probe without install, install chosen available version, keep at-or-above, replace strictly newer, enforce the declared minimum, report the installed version); FORGEL.md project rules (deterministic orchestrator; documentation and code own the contract); AGENTS.md (process rules live in code, not prose).
external_dependencies.evidence: The engine is not a repository of this project: the project repository list contains only 'main: application' and 'code: application', and no vendored engine installer source or engine version-output fixture is present in the inspected repository context. The contract is therefore taken from the specification itself, which states: 'It is idempotent by comparing the installed engine against the version the configured engine source provides: no engine installs it, an installed engine at or above the available one is kept untouched, a strictly newer available engine replaces it, and the finished result always satisfies the declared minimum, failing with an actionable message when it cannot' and 'the run reports which engine version is installed'. FORGEL.md adds 'The orchestrator is deterministic; the LLM works only inside a step', so the probe/install/report surface must be a deterministic local seam rather than a real download. The stub below implements exactly those states and no other interface.

external_dependencies.name: engine distribution channel reached by the configured source
external_dependencies.interface: The client passes the configured engine source (the documented default, overridable in configuration) straight through to the engine installer; it never opens its own transport for the engine. The channel resolves a source to the set of published engine versions, exposes the newest one for probing, and yields an installable artifact for an exact version. In tests the channel is an in-memory catalogue; no HTTP, DNS, credentials or filesystem outside the tmp path are involved.
external_dependencies.docs: Task specification in the repository: 'The default engine source is a documented configuration' and the client keeps using the same channel and fetch mechanism it already uses today for the client; the engine is obtained through the engine's own installation, not through a new channel invented here. Client user documentation of the current installation channel (referenced by the dependency contract).
external_dependencies.evidence: The specification states the channel is a configuration value, not new code: 'The default engine source is a documented configuration', and the dependency contract for this repository states 'The client's installation keeps using the same channel and fetch mechanism it uses today for the client; the engine is obtained through the engine's own installation, not through a new channel invented here.' No channel client, release-fetch helper or network fixture for engine artifacts exists in the inspected repository context, and the project repository list ('main: application', 'code: application') contains no channel repository, so the transport is stubbed as a deterministic in-memory catalogue that the client reaches only through the installer seam above. FORGEL.md: 'The orchestrator is deterministic', which rules out a live fetch in tests.
